Title: I think I used the Hermes Agent wrong
Description: Around three weeks ago, I made the switch from OpenClaw. The idea of a self-learning AI agent (as Nous Research advertises it) hooked me. It also matches how I think about AI agents: I want them to grow with me. I installed the Hermes Agent and gave it a try.

Title: Getting 50 GB/s Back Out of the ANE
Description: An RTL performance erratum in the Apple M3 Neural Engine throttles DRAM weight streaming throughput down to 17–19 GB/s from the nominal 45–60 GB/s, whenever the total weight size is an integer multiple of 1 MiB, which currently affects 7 of ANEMLL’s 15 models. Avoiding the problematic path in the kernel DMA engine's speculative prefetch ring increased Llama 3.2 1B token throughput from 10.0 to 24.3 tokens/s (DRAM usage from 24.7 to 60.0 GB/s), and Qwen3-8B from 1.36 to 2.97 tokens/s (DRAM usage from 22.4 to 48.7 GB/s).

Title: ID design and primary keys, pt. 1
Description:
Author: Alexey Makhotkin squadette@gmail.com, (~2300 words)
This is the first part of a systematic discussion of primary keys in database design. As usual, we present the material in a way that deviates from the traditional approach.
This is basically a bonus chapter from the “Database Design Book”. The goal of this text is to teach you how to design your primary keys based on business requirements.
In part 1, we begin at the logical level.

Title: The new addiction to working all the time
Description:
We’re all so excited about the newest capabilities of each released AI model that we’re forgetting the consequences of having access to such an amazing tool, and the possibility of being able to do so much so fast.
I know people who go to the gym and still have their phones connected so they can keep sending prompts to their laptops. I’m guilty myself of opening ChatGPT with audio mode in my car while I’m driving alone to chat about projects.
